newsitem.title: USA: Fla lawyer seeks punitive damages in tobacco case.
newsitem.headline: Fla lawyer seeks punitive damages in tobacco case.

text.p: An attorney for a deceased smoker whose estate filed a wrongful death suit against R.J. Reynolds asked a judge Thursday to allow him to seek punitive damages against the tobacco company.

Norwood "Woody" Wilner, a Jacksonville attorney who has filed hundreds of product-liability and wrongful-death cases against tobacco companies in Florida courts, argued that the lawsuit filed by deceased smoker Jean Connor met the state's standard for punitive damages.
He cited thousands of documents purported to show cigarettes are a dangerous and defective product, which he intended to present when the case goes to trial April 7.

Attorneys in Wilner's office said if the motion was granted, it would mark the first time an individual plaintiff in a Florida tobacco case was allowed to seek punitive damages against a tobacco company.
Circuit Judge Bernard Nachman gave Wilner a week to cull and submit 15 documents to the court and another week for R.J. Reynolds to respond before issuing a ruling on the motion.

Connor, who died of lung cancer in the fall of 1995, filed the product liability lawsuit shortly before her death. After her death it became a wrongful death suit filed by her sister, Dana Raulerson, on behalf of Connor's estate.
Attorney Paul Crist, representing R.J. Reynolds, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, argued that the case did not meet the state's standard for punitive damages.

Last August, one of Wilner's clients, Grady Carter of Orange Park, Florida, and his wife won a $750,000 jury award in his product-liability lawsuit against B.A.T Industries Plc's Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp.
